title: The critical dimension for one-phase Bernoulli minimizers
main_claim: d_*=7: every nonzero one-homogeneous global minimizer of the Alt–Caffarelli one-phase energy in R^d, d<=6, is flat. Consequences: the singular set is empty for n<=6, locally finite for n=7, and has Hausdorff dimension <= n-7, which is sharp. Proof outline: (1) reduce a hypothetical first nonflat cone in dimension 5 or 6 to a smooth link in S^5, suspending a 5D cone, which adds two tips. (2) Build a test h = w^a sqrt(f) and a flux field Z from the normalized Hessian. The targets are div Z >= |grad h|^2 + 4h^2 + eps*w^{2a} and N.Z + H h^2 >= 0, both certified by an exact rational sum-of-squares/remainder certificate. (3) Weighted Bochner cutoffs at Hessian zeros and at the tips contradict spherical stability.

issues.description: The main inequality depends entirely on a large finite computation: 231 Table I rows, 557 Gram rows, 1714 remainder keys. The bundled reproduce.py passed, and I independently re-checked the final rational arithmetic (D0 <= Dbar entrywise, the four slacks, delta*). That the code faithfully implements the manuscript formulas (D_l rules, the C/G contractions, the coefficients 2a-1, 2a+1, 2a) rests on the authors' two engines; their README says so explicitly. My own independent numerical evaluation of I and S from the tables was stopped at the background time limit before printing any result.

- Divergence identity and its q coefficients; square completion giving |∇h|²; the boundary flux identity N·Z + Hh² = w^{2a+1}S; the reflection parity argument.
- Weighted Bochner absorption, which needs 4a-2>0; dominated convergence at Hessian zeros and at the tips (s^{2-2a} integrable, mass ∫ sin^{4-2a} > 0).
